scope_note: Flinn and Womack give 41 people across the 100 chamber ascents. Ascents repeat within subjects.
Reported ascents to altitudes above 35,000 ft. The original ascertainment and per-ascent histories are unavailable.
The cited outcome is stopping an ascent because of DCS. The original total symptomatic count and the follow-up of other ascents are unknown.
Fifteen ascents occur in the same sentence as the visual findings. The cited account lacks the subset selection and linkage of events to ascents.
Eight observations are a recurrent symptom count. No numerator of distinct scotoma-positive ascents is given.
Six people are described with scotomas in the quoted visual subset. The number assessed in that subset is unavailable.
Only a rounded rate is quoted. The visual definitions also cover other symptoms such as blurred vision and diplopia. The primary case-level count is unavailable.
The denominator is selected collapse cases with no preceding dysbarism symptoms. This is a case-conditional symptom count.
The cited assessment uses 16 susceptible subjects. The study's broader historical reported affected total is 17. The reason for the smaller comparison denominator is unknown.
Historical selected reference group described as non-susceptible. Original matching, assessment and ascertainment remain unverified.
